table.name: airlines
table.purpose: Lookup table of airlines; each row is one airline, referenced by the flights table.

col_001.name: airline_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each airline. Referenced by flights.col_001 (many flights to one airline).

col_002.name: airline_name
col_002.description: Full, official airline name (e.g. 'Delta Airlines', 'US Airways'). Unique per row.

col_003.name: airline_abbreviation
col_003.description: Short/common airline name or brand abbreviation (e.g. 'USAir' for 'US Airways', 'JetBlue' for 'JetBlue Airways').

col_004.name: country
col_004.description: Country of the airline; all 12 rows are 'USA'. Could also be a region code, but 'USA' strongly suggests country.

table.name: airports
table.purpose: Reference table of airports (one row per airport), keyed by IATA/airport code, referenced by the flights table for origin and destination airports. All airports are in the United States.

col_001.name: city
col_001.description: Name of the city (or locality) served by the airport, e.g. 'Albany', 'Anchorage'. Values have trailing spaces.

col_002.name: airport_code
col_002.description: Primary key. Three-letter airport code (IATA/FAA code), e.g. 'APN' for Alpena. Referenced by flights columns col_003 and col_004 (origin/destination airport).

col_003.name: airport_name
col_003.description: Full name of the airport, e.g. 'Alpena County Regional', 'Outagamie County'. Sometimes equals the city name; values have trailing spaces.

col_004.name: country
col_004.description: Country name; constant 'United States' in this data.

col_005.name: country_code
col_005.description: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), 'US' for all rows; one value has a trailing space ('US ').

table.name: flights
table.purpose: One row per flight: which airline operates it, a flight number, and the origin and destination airports (US domestic flights).

col_001.name: airline_id
col_001.description: References airlines.col_001; identifies the operating carrier (12 airlines, e.g. 2=US Airways, 4=Southwest, 8=JetBlue, 11=Allegiant, 12=Virgin America).

col_002.name: flight_number
col_002.description: Flight number, 2-1535, unique per airline-airport combination in this sample (836 distinct over 1200 rows). No join targets found, so this reading is inferred from range and uniqueness; it could also be an internal route/flight ID.

col_003.name: origin_airport_code
col_003.description: IATA airport code (leading space present in stored values) referencing airports.col_002; the flight's origin airport (e.g. APN=Alpena, ATW=Appleton).

col_004.name: destination_airport_code
col_004.description: IATA airport code (leading space present in stored values) referencing airports.col_002, which is the airports table's primary key; identifies the flight's destination airport. Origin vs destination assignment between col_003/col_004 remains tentative (symmetric distributions), but the join confirms this is one of the two endpoint airports.
